name: Airbrush Surrealism
summary: Surreal airbrushed illustration: supersaturated colour, floating or juxtaposed objects, chrome surfaces, lightning and X-ray cut-aways. It lived on album covers, pulp science fiction and fantasy, and pin-up chrome robots.

philosophy.core_thesis: A dream can be rendered as a polished object: the airbrush gives an impossible scene the smooth, lit surface of a photograph.
design_principles: Build every form with airbrushed gradients and no visible stroke: a sphere or a tube holds a smooth tonal run of 8 to 12 steps from highlight to core shadow.
Render chrome and metal with a sharp horizon line in the reflection: a sky band over a dark ground band, split at 50% of the form height.
Place 2 to 4 unrelated objects in one scene, juxtaposed or floating, with a clear gap of 5 to 15% of the picture between them.
Raise saturation to the top of the range in the sky and in glows: use 3 to 5 hues, such as electric blue, magenta and orange, at full chroma.
Cut hard edges with masking film: each shape has a crisp edge of 0.5mm or less, and each glow has a soft edge of 20 to 60mm.
Add one light effect, such as a lightning bolt, a lens flare or a halo, that crosses 30 to 50% of the picture.
Show the inside of a body or a machine in one X-ray cut-away, with the outer skin stopped at a clean line.
Set the horizon at 1/3 from the bottom, in a flat plain or a sea, so that the objects stand in a deep, empty space.
anti_patterns: Visible brush strokes and impasto in the paint
Soft, hazy focus with no crisp mask edge
A single, realistic scene with no impossible element
Neon grid, wireframe and digital glow from later computer imagery
Hand-drawn contour lines of uniform weight around each form
Flat poster colour with no gradient on the forms

composition.layout: A centred or slightly off-centre hero object on a deep plain or sea horizon, with secondary objects floating in the sky at 2 to 3 scales.
composition.focal_point: The brightest highlight or the lightning strike, placed at 1/3 from the top and 1/3 from one side.
composition.format: A square 30 by 30cm album sleeve (1:1), a pulp cover of 2:3, or a landscape 3:2; the main object may be cut by the edge by up to 10%.

principles.rule: Put the highest contrast and the sharpest highlight on one object, which fills 25 to 40% of the picture.
Show 3 to 4 planes: a foreground object, a mid-ground object, a horizon band and a sky gradient of 40% of the height.
Set a dark core shadow (below 15% lightness) against a specular highlight (above 90%) on the same form.
Leave 25 to 35% of the picture as open sky or sea, filled by a smooth gradient and not by detail.
Make the scale wrong on purpose: an object at 3 to 10 times its natural size next to a small one.

palette.strategy: Supersaturated gradients: a deep ultramarine or black sky that glows into magenta, orange and cyan at the horizon, with chrome that reflects the same hues.
palette.distribution: Dark sky and ground 40–50%, saturated gradient glow 25–30%, chrome and highlight neutrals 15–20%, one hot accent under 10%.
palette.ground: Smooth white illustration board or a gessoed panel, sealed so that the spray lies flat and even.

brushwork_and_medium.medium: Liquid acrylic, gouache and dye, sprayed through an airbrush at 20 to 40 psi, with masking film and frisket to hold the edges.
brushwork_and_medium.support: Illustration board or gessoed hardboard, from 30 by 30cm to 60 by 90cm; a final fix with a clear varnish.
brushwork_and_medium.brushwork: No brush stroke shows. The spray builds in thin layers of 10 to 30 passes; a fine brush adds only specular dots of 1 to 2mm.
brushwork_and_medium.paint_handling: Paint goes on thin and transparent, and each mask is cut, sprayed and removed in turn; tone builds by repeat passes and not by thick paint.
brushwork_and_medium.edges: Crisp, knife-cut edges on solid objects and soft, 20 to 60mm spray edges on glow, cloud and haze; the two meet in each picture.

light_and_modelling.light: A strong, single key light with a rim light of a second colour; the highlights are specular and clipped at white.
light_and_modelling.modelling: Form comes from smooth gradients, with a sharp reflection line on metal and a glossy highlight on every curved surface.
light_and_modelling.shadow: Core shadows run to near black; cast shadows are soft ovals under floating objects at 20 to 30% opacity.
light_and_modelling.temperature: Cool blues in the sky and shadows against warm orange and magenta in glows; chrome picks up both.

subject.typical: Album covers, pulp science fiction and fantasy, pin-up chrome robots, floating eyes and planets, lightning, skulls, spacecraft and technical cut-aways.
subject.figure_scale: The hero object fills 25–50% of the height; a figure or robot may reach 70–90% on a pin-up or a pulp cover.
subject.treatment: Idealised and polished: bodies and machines are smooth, symmetrical and glossy, with no wear and no visible texture.

surface.finish: Glossy and seamless, as a photograph; varnish adds a uniform sheen.
surface.texture: No texture: a fine spray grain visible only at 10 times magnification.

reference_works.note: The museum catalogue holds few airbrush works of the period; these ids were checked against the Art Institute of Chicago API. Man Ray's 1919 aerograph is the earliest ancestor. Look at the museum page for the image and its licence; none is flagged public domain.

emotion.target_response: Glossy wonder with a hint of menace: the viewer looks at an impossible object that seems real enough to touch.

use_cases: science fiction and fantasy book covers
avoid_when: The brief asks for a loose, painterly or hand-made look.
The subject is a quiet, realistic scene with no impossible element.

modifiers.how: Cut the gradients to 3 flat steps, add a 3px outline and halftone dots; keep the saturated palette and the floating objects.
Reduce the glow to one warm light source, deepen the shadows to near black, and drop the chrome; keep the smooth surface and the single focal object.
Replace the sprayed gradients with visible touches of 5–15mm and let the edges break; keep the colour heat of the sky.

brush_size.note: The airbrush leaves no stroke, so the size stays near 0.
